question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's set $u=\ln\left(5 \left(\frac{x}{1}\right)\right).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,1\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $\frac{e}{5}$ | $\frac{e^{4}}{5}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $4$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}\int_{\frac{e}{5}}^{\frac{e^{4}}{5}}\frac{1}{\left(\frac{x}{1}\right)\operatorname{ln}(5\left(\frac{x}{1}\right))}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{2}{3}\int_{\frac{e}{5}}^{\frac{e^{4}}{5}}\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}(5\left(\frac{x}{1}\right))}\cdot \frac{1}{\left(\frac{x}{1}\right)}\,\text{d}x \\ & =\frac{2}{3}\int_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\ & =\frac{2}{3}\cdot\left((\operatorname{ln}Abs(u))\right)|_{1}^{4} \\ & =\frac{2}{3}\cdot\left(\operatorname{ln}4-\operatorname{ln}1\right) \\ & =\frac{2}{3}\cdot\left(\operatorname{ln}4\right)\end{aligned}
$$
